newsitem.title: USA: Amtrak says near signing long-term power contracts.
newsitem.headline: Amtrak says near signing long-term power contracts.

text.p: Amtrak is close to signing purchase contracts for the electricity used to move its trains between New York and Washington DC, company officials said.
"We're hoping it will happen soon. We're looking at final bids," an Amtrak spokeswoman said, but declined to say when the when the agreements likely would be finalized.
Amtrak this summer issued a tender soliciting bids to power the 250-mile electrified segment of its main Northeast Corridor line.
"We have been analyzing and working with the group of lowest bidders," said Amy Linden, vice-president for business development.
The request for proposal (RFP) details requirements for electricity supplies in two-, three-, four- and five-year blocks. It seeks annual delivery of 600 million kilowatt-hour (KWh) of electricity.
Linden declined to disclose the number of final bidders with whom Amtrak has been negotiating.
"We'll be going with one," she replied when asked how many bidders would be awarded.

Amtrak plans to use about half of the supply to serve its own trains and resell the rest to three commuter railways--the Maryland Rail Commuter (MARC), New Jersey Transit Authority (NJT), and Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority (SEPTA).
Linden said the RFP is one of Amtrak's first steps toward cutting power costs on its Northeast Corridor line as it converts the entire route to electricity.
So far the line is electrified only from Washington to New York, though it terminates farther north in Boston.
"This is just for traction power. We're still looking to reduce power cost for the entire line," Linden said.
Amtrak said it would likely be issuing more RFPs following completion of electrification of the Northeast Corridor in 1999.
